Maya (PM): quick decision needed — can we narrow the toolkit slice for the next 2-week sprint? I propose we prioritize eval-triggered alerts + a lightweight quantization recommendation path. This hits most customer asks and reduces infra scope.

Liam (Eng): +1 on narrowing. Full batching + KV cache infra is >2w. Eval alerts + simple recs (heuristic rules) is doable. Need alignment on SLOs and how noisy the alerts can be.

Sanjay (ML Eng): Agree. For eval-triggered alerts we need: baseline eval set, signal thresholds, and a small storage for recent prompt/responses to compute regression. We can prototype with a daily job + nearline alerts before realtime.

Rachel (Customer Success): Customers pressing for "early regression alerts" (Cust A, Cust C). They prefer alerts tied to semantic evals (concordance) rather than raw perplexity. If we can ship a configurable threshold and email+Slack hooks, that'll satisfy most.

Eva (Research): Recommend these initial success metrics: alert = true positive rate >= 70% on flagged regressions, false positive rate < 15% on calibration set. Also include a manual triage UI for early pilots.

Liam (Eng): technical constraints: realtime detection + streaming would require hooking into runtime and extra cost. If we start with nearline (5-15m) we avoid kernel changes and can reuse eval infra. Also quant recs: we can return "recommended profile" (e.g., fp16-safe, int8-light) but not apply automatic quantization yet.

Maya (PM): proposed acceptance criteria (draft):
```
- Eval-alerts: configurable eval suite ingestion, threshold config UI, Slack/email webhook delivery.
- Pilot: onboard 2 customers with manual triage for 2 weeks.
- Quant recs: API that returns one of {none, conservative-int8, aggressive-int8} with explanation and perf/cost delta estimate.
- No mandatory runtime changes for pilot (nearline allowed).
```

Rachel (Customer Success): I'll line up Cust A + Cust B for pilots and give them an intake form. They want ETA and rollback plan though.

Liam (Eng): ETA: nearline eval-alert prototype + webhook: 2w. Quant recs API: 1w for a simple rule engine + perf table. Need an owner for rollout scripts.

Sanjay (ML Eng): I'll own the eval signal definitions and write the initial concordance checks. Will need sample prompts from customers and a holdout set.

Maya (PM): Owners: Liam (eng) prototype + infra checklist, Sanjay (ML) signals, Rachel (CS) pilot customers, Eva (research) metric validation. Ops-bot: @ops-bot create a ticket for infra risk assessment.

ops-bot: created ticket PRODUCT-9832: "infra-risk: eval-alerts nearline prototype" assigned to eng-infra. Link: https://redwood.internal/issue/PRODUCT-9832

Eva (Research): Quick note — instrument a small "confidence decay" metric for quant recs so we can detect model-output mismatch after model variant swap. Helps avoid bad recommendations.

Maya (PM): decision summary: ship eval-triggered alerts (nearline) + quant recommendation API for pilot. Defer full batching/KV cache work to next cycle unless a customer commits to dedicated capacity. Anyone object?

Liam (Eng): no objections. :+1:

Sanjay (ML Eng): no objections. happy to iterate on thresholds. :thumbsup:

Rachel (Customer Success): sounds good. I'll share pilot intake by EOD.

Maya (PM): thanks — I'll update the roadmap doc and create the sprint card. Link: https://docs.redwood/intern/optimize/toolkit/sprint-slice-1766

Liam (Eng): small follow-up: can we add a guardrail in the API to mark "pilot mode" so recs are flagged as suggestions, not enforced? that reduces risk for customers.

Maya (PM): yes — add "pilot_mode": true flag to the API contract. We'll add to acceptance criteria.

Sanjay (ML Eng): scheduling note — need 1 day with Cust A to collect prompts and 1 day for baseline eval run. I'll coordinate with Rachel.

Maya (PM): final: action items posted to the sprint card. We'll triage infra work if PRODUCT-9832 surfaces blockers. Thanks team. :rocket:
